data.name: Majestic Trials
data.detailed_description:
Unfortunately, there are rather a lot of wizards. If you want to join the Majestic Few, be prepared to enter the Majestic Trials.

Majestic Trials is a turn-based fantasy tactical game where you must compete in increasingly challenging trials to earn your place within the Majestic Citadel.


To succeed you will need help. A variety of creatures, mundane, magical and monstrous will be available, summoned with your magic or found and 'befriended'. Use their abilities to scout the area and combat your opponents and their servants, avoiding confrontations that could otherwise bring a swift end to your efforts to join the Majestic Few.



Discover forgotten spells to improve your character, find valuable and powerful treasures and try to prevent your opponents from doing the same. Each trial provides opportunities to improve yourself before the next trial, assuming of course that you survive that trial! You will need to explore every nook and every cranny of an area thoroughly.





  • Choose a wizard to play from a large selection and customise their starting spells.
  • Enter varied trials within unique fantasy locations with different challenges and opponents. Face zombie pirates on creaky docks, scuttling giant spiders in dank caves, skeletal warriors in abandoned fortresses and much more.


  • There are dozens of different types of creatures to be found and befriended or summoned with your magic.


  • Use the terrain features in a trial to your advantage. Hide behind trees or set them on fire!
  • Discover new spells and find useful treasure to help improve your character between trials.


  • Improve your wizard the way you want to after a successful trial.
  • Do favours for the Majestic Few. They don't all like each other and none of them want to be the one who loses their place to which-ever wizard comes out on top in the trials.

data.short_description: Majestic Trials is a turn-based fantasy tactical game where you are a wizard that competes in increasingly challenging trials to earn your place within an elite mage cabal. Summon and befriend dozens of different creatures to aid you, and specialise in schools to learn a variety of spells.

reviews.review:
[h1]IN A WORD: [b]MAYBE[/b][/h1]
[h1]IN A NUTSHELL:[/h1]
[quote=]
[b]WHAT TO EXPECT:[/b] Indie made. Old school look and feel. Campaign of 13x trials or a single one. Table-top style adventure mixed with dungeon crawling gameplay. Fantasy setting. Lite rogue-like structure. Spellcasting main character. Customisation of 6x stats and a repertoire of spells. Party turn-based tactics with emphasis on magic and ally attacks. Lite RPG elements, with XP spent on stats and spell-casting capabilities. Collect loot to reverse-engineer into spells. Large bestiary of creatures to charm, summon or kill. Retro hand-drawn visuals and midi sound-effects. Lite dynamic elements add some replayability. Single-player only.
[hr][/hr][b]ACHIEVEMENTS:[/b] Straightforward. Requires multiple replays.
[b]STEAM SUPPORT:[/b] Trading Cards.
[b]STATUS:[/b] Released but needs some QoL and more features.
[b]FOR WHOM[/b] Fans of retro turn-based strategy games.
[b]WHEN TO BUY:[/b] Overpriced. Get on a good sale.[/quote]

[i]More info below....[/i]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2767655645
[h1]THE LOWDOWN:[/h1]
Majestic Trials (MT) is an old school, turn-based adventure with elements of RPG, strategy and combat. It is has a lite rogue-like structure, with a touch of dungeon crawling and is remindful of related games from the past. Delivers retro style visuals that are hand-crafted and midi-made sound-effects that highlight mostly spell-casting and combat actions. The overall goal is to complete favours for spell-casters known as the Majestic Few, across numerous trials, with the aim of eventually replacing one of these.

[b]Character Customisation[/b]
Players take on the role of a spell-caster. Character customisation involves defining a name and appearance. Points are allocated to a handful of core stats, while known spells are allocated to slots in the character's spell library. From these individual instances of each spell are assigned to slots in a spell-book, where only these can be cast during a trial. Spells can be assigned once or a multiple times.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
MT takes place as a single trial or a campaign of sequential ones. In campaign mode each trial can be played on a choice of maps. One or more quests from up to five are offered by the Majestic Few as the goal of the trial. The core part of gameplays requires charming or summoning a party of NPC allies that are represented as counters, to explore huge square-tiled maps viewed from the top-down. 

[b]Combat[/b]
Spells are the caster's main form of tactical combat. Along with the number of ranged offensive spells such as fireball and lightning, they are able to charm or summon creatures to fight on their behalf. Some creatures and other NPCs possess their own tactical abilities, ranged and/or melee attacks that can apply special conditions on their targets. Such as knock-down, poison or disease. Enemy wizards have their own repertoire of spells to use against your party. In addition aspects of combat include line-of-sight for spell-casting or ranged attacks. RNG affects the to-hit chance of all attacks. Warding affects if a spell has any impact on its target.

[h1]THE GOOD:[/h1]
+ REPLAYABLE CAMPAIGN: 13x trials with different maps for each to play and up to five selectable quests per trial.
+ DYNAMIC ELEMENTS: Some randomisation of map elements: Quests, NPCs, layout, loot containers and spawn locations.
+ SIZEABLE BESTIARY: Very good with a good variety of NPCs and creatures. Lots to charm and summon, and control.
+ MULTIPLE STRATEGIES: Can create and save multiple wizards. Adopt one of nine magic schools. Use at least two separate styles or various mixes of spells.

[h1]THE BAD:[/h1]
- UNBALANCED: Some unbalanced encounters. Can meet overpowered enemies. Which leads to quick death.
- NEEDS QOL: GUI is in need of QoL and could do with adding more information such as unit capabilities, spell information etc.
- BETTER PROGRESSION: No enhancements/progression for spells or ability to save some of the party from the previous trial.
- FIDDLY CONTROLS. A few keyboard commands are not working or missing: cycle to next ally, end current turn. Navigating the map is a pain. Is done only by mouse. No arrow key shortcuts to move a hex at a time. Characters can also lose focus with the mouse and need reacquiring. Again no key, must be done with the mouse.
- INVENTORY: Cumbersome, basic and overly fiddly when trying to transfer items between allies. Could have done with a global model instead.

[h1]AND THE REST:[/h1]
* CHARACTER CUSTOMISATION: Fair but needs to be expanded with a few more aspects to level. i.e. specific abilities to compliment the magic stuff
* MECHANICS: Overall decent. Different attacks. Conditions inflicted on opponents. Locked doors. Line of Sight. Riding some animals. Could have done with more such as a shared inventory pool. Cant see if every container seen has been opened. Charmed or summoned NPCs cannot collect items. Picking up items takes too long. Spells are centred on summoning, charming NPCs and buffing them. A few attack spells.
* SLOW PLAY: The use of action points provides greater tactical options but slows down the fluidity of gameplay.
* LOW PRODUCTION VALUES: Retro graphics, no voice acting, midi sound-effects may be an issue for some gamers. Though the graphics actually appealed to me.
* CHAOTIC LEARNING CURVE: Lacks the info to give it an easy learning curve. While not difficult mistakes can be made that are fatal.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2765033998
[h1]ANALYSIS:[/h1]
Compared to other games in its genre, it is fair but does not possess much that would make it stand out. However a fair level of thought has gone into its design and if you are the type of gamer that enjoys a casual retro experience, it has a number of facets that could be appealing.

[h1]VERDICT:[/h1]
Majestic Trials has that nostalgic quality that may appeal to gamers interested in seeing how a game from the 80s would have played like. It retains a solid design and should be easy enough to get into. However it really needed additional features to increase the tactical aspect of the game and increase its depth, and its complexity. Some QoL to the GUI impart more information and controls to stop it from playing a little sluggishly.

Those of you who are attracted to it should perhaps wait for a good sale because it does not have the depth of features it should have at the current price. That is why I believe this is a MAYBE purchase rather than an emphatic one. Only if you like what you see and read.
